title: Dense Cohen–Macaulay locus in a finite type algebra over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $A$ be a commutative finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. The set of prime ideals $\mathfrak q\subset A$ for which the local ring $A_{\mathfrak q}$ is Cohen–Macaulay (that is, Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and its depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] equals its Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]) is a dense open subset of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Equivalently, every nonempty open subset of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ contains a prime $\mathfrak q$ with Cohen–Macaulay localization $A_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Tag 00RG, label lemma-generic-CM (using Tag 00RF for openness and the minimal-prime argument)

proof.text: Let $U$ be the set in the statement. Consider the structure morphism $f:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Because $k$ is a field, the $k$-module $A$ is flat. The field $k$ is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$, both finitely generated. Apply the finite-type-over-Noetherian finite-presentation theorem to $R=k$ and $S=A$ to obtain that $A$ is finitely presented over $k$. Thus $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. The existing general fibre Cohen–Macaulay-locus theorem makes the locus where the fibre depth equals fibre Krull dimension open. Here the only fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and the affine-stalk localization theorem identifies its local ring at $\mathfrak q$ with $A_{\mathfrak q}$. The finite-type Noetherian theorem followed by the localization-Noetherian theorem shows every $A_{\mathfrak q}$ is Noetherian, so this depth-equals-dimension locus is exactly $U$. Hence $U$ is open.

source.place: Tag 00RF (openness), as used in Tag 00RG; the general fibre-locus formulation is the existing Tag 045U node; finite presentation from Tag 00FP, label lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q$ be a minimal prime of $A$. By the prime-localization correspondence, primes of $A_{\mathfrak q}$ correspond to primes of $A$ contained in $\mathfrak q$, so minimality leaves only $\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak q}$; the Krull-dimension definition therefore gives $\dim A_{\mathfrak q}=0$. The ring $A_{\mathfrak q}$ is Noetherian by Step 1. Its sole prime is minimal, so the Noetherian minimal-prime-associated theorem supplies an associated-prime witness for $\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak q}$. Regard $A_{\mathfrak q}$ as a finite module over itself. The depth-bound theorem for an associated prime gives $\operatorname{depth}(A_{\mathfrak q})\leq\dim(A_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak q})=0$. The empty regular sequence gives depth at least zero from the depth definition, hence depth equals dimension. This argument allows a nonzero nilpotent maximal ideal (for example $k[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$), so it does not infer that the maximal ideal is zero. Thus every minimal-prime point lies in $U$.

source.place: Tag 00RG proof, sentence that minimal-prime local rings are Cohen–Macaulay, corrected using Tags 05BV and 0BK4

proof.text: The minimal-prime density lemma says that every nonempty open subset of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ contains a minimal-prime point. Since Step 1 makes $U$ open and Step 2 puts every minimal-prime point in $U$, every nonempty open meets $U$. Therefore $U$ is dense, proving the equivalent formulation as well.

source.place: Tag 00RG proof, final minimal-prime density argument
